transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Morgan (Stratus CTO), Derek Huang (Lead ML Eng), Maria Torres (Security), Liam Reed (Product)

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, appreciate it. quick intros?
[00:00:06] Ava: Hi, Ava, CTO at Stratus, we run the inference platform for our analytics product, thanks for joining.
[00:00:12] Derek: Derek, lead ML eng, i'll be building the POC and running the benchmarks.
[00:00:16] Maria: Maria, security and compliance. I'll be reviewing data flows and encryption.
[00:00:21] Jordan: Awesome, i'm Jordan AE, and Samir is our solutions engineer who's going to lead tech details. Samir?
[00:00:27] Samir: Hey all, thanks. quick agenda: align success criteria, sizing, benchmarks, and integration plan — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool-calling and structured output.
[00:00:39] Ava: Sound good. For context, we're evaluating Redwood because we need lower latency than our current hosted provider and better cost predictability. Also we need a path to VPC or dedicated for data residency.
[00:00:50] Jordan: Got it. can you walk through current traffic and constraints?
[00:00:54] Derek: Sure — production is variable; peak QPS for our realtime annotator is about 40 requests/sec, each request averages ~120 tokens input and we expect 1.2x tokens output on average. For batch embedding jobs, we do ~50k vectors/day. Latency SLO for realtime is 200ms p50 and p99 under 800ms.
[00:01:12] Samir: That's helpful. when you say 200ms p50, is that end-to-end from client to client, including network? or server-side inference only?
[00:01:19] Derek: End-to-end for our app; but for the POC we want to measure Redwood server-side latency and tail, so we can subtract network overhead.
[00:01:27] Jordan: Great — so proposed success criteria?
[00:01:31] Ava: Primary: server-side p50 < 120ms, p99 < 600ms for our typical prompt sizes. Secondary: cost per 1k tokens less than our current baseline, and no regression in answer quality for our prompt set. Also security sign-off: keys with KMS and audit logs.
[00:01:46] Samir: Noted. we'll test with your prompt set and also run an A/B with your quality evals. can you share the eval prompts?
[00:01:53] Derek: Yes will share. we'll also want to validate function/tool-calling since our app uses structured actions: model calls a tool with a JSON payload.
[00:02:02] Samir: Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function calling patterns; we have examples in the SDK that show typed JSON outputs and automatic function invocation. For POC we'll provide a small harness that shows both the streaming token path and the function-calling flow.
[00:02:16] Maria: On security: we need assurance about data retention, encryption at rest, and in transit. if you provide a dedicated or private deployment, what are the key controls?
[00:02:25] Jordan: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and customer-managed KMS integration; logs can be routed to your SIEM and we keep audit logs — we'll share SOC 2 docs. For hosted tests, data is encrypted at rest and we have retention policies you can configure.
[00:02:40] Maria: Ok please share SOC2 summary and KMS integration guide.
[00:02:44] Jordan: Will do.
[00:02:47] Ava: timeline — we want to decision in two weeks and POC to run for 2-3 weeks after kickoff. Is that feasible?
[00:02:54] Samir: Yes. Proposed timeline: Jordan sends POC proposal + pricing in 2 business days; once approved we do a technical kickoff week of July 6, run bench and integration for two weeks, then a wrap with results.
[00:03:08] Derek: That works. question about integration: we use a Node + Python stack and currently call OpenAI API. how similar will integration be?
[00:03:17] Samir: The endpoints are OpenAI-compatible for the hosted API: same request/response shapes, same function-calling semantics. We also provide first-class SDKs in Node and Python with helpers for streaming, retry, and structured outputs. For Dedicated/Private the API surface is identical, it's mostly auth and network differences.
[00:03:32] Derek: Great — will the SDKs have helpers for model selection, quantization profile, and batching?
[00:03:37] Samir: Yes, the SDK exposes model config flags and batching helpers; for the POC we'll annotate recommended model/quantization profiles based on your prompt lengths. We can run two profiles: low-latency (smaller quantized model) and high-quality (larger fp16 model) to compare.
[00:03:52] Ava: And about cost: how granular is billing? we want cost per token plus reserved capacity options.
[00:03:58] Jordan: Hosted is per-token; Dedicated has reserved capacity and predictable monthly commits. For the POC we'll show estimated unit economics for both options.
[00:04:06] Derek: Benchmarks — what will you run out of the box?
[00:04:09] Samir: We'll provide a benchmark harness: single-shot latency tests across 95/99 percentiles, throughput tests increasing concurrency to emulate your 40 QPS and spikes, and cost modeling. We'll run both streaming and non-streaming flows, and the function-calling path. We'll need a representative prompt set and a few sample payloads.
[00:04:26] Ava: We'll deliver ~200 sample prompts and the evaluation harness next week.
[00:04:30] Maria: For security tests, we want to ensure no logs persist beyond retention, and that PII is not stored. Can the POC be in a dedicated tenant?
[00:04:39] Jordan: For POC we can spin up an isolated tenant in hosted or use a Dedicated eval node depending on timing. For quick tests hosted isolated tenant with strict retention should be okay; for later we can move to Dedicated.
[00:04:50] Derek: One more on structured output: our app expects the model to return a JSON with keys action, args where args is a typed object. Can Redwood enforce schema validation and return a structured parse?
[00:05:00] Samir: We support function definitions similar to OpenAI — you can define parameter schemas and models will attempt to return JSON that conforms. Our SDK has a post-parse validator and we can run a lightweight schema-check at the gateway and report parsing rates. For POC we'll measure parse success rates and fallback frequency.
[00:05:16] Ava: Excellent. Regarding endpoints: do you expose an embeddings-only endpoint or is that via same API?
[00:05:22] Samir: Same API surface but different routes — embeddings and completions/Chat. For embeddings we can offer bulk batching to reduce cost. We'll include embedding throughput guidance in the benchmark.
[00:05:32] Derek: For embeddings we need 50k vectors/day, some deduping, and we use cosine similarity in our pipeline. Any constraints?
[00:05:38] Samir: No constraints; we'll size GPU memory for embedding model and recommend batching. We'll provide estimated token/second and concurrency to meet your latency/cost targets.
[00:05:47] Maria: For audit, who has access to logs? We need roles and RBAC.
[00:05:52] Jordan: We have RBAC in the Console — you can assign roles and we support SAML/SSO for enterprise. Access to audit logs can be restricted to specific roles. We'll include a snippet of RBAC mappings.
[00:06:03] Ava: Good. any blockers on our side to start?
[00:06:06] Derek: We'll need NDA signed and a small legal review for data residency. Also will need to provision sample keys for benchmark to hit the hosted endpoint.
[00:06:15] Jordan: NDA is standard — i'll send that with the POC proposal.
[00:06:18] Samir: On tech specifics — for the benchmark script we'll include both OpenAI-compatible curl examples and SDK snippets (Node/Python). We'll also provide a Dockerized harness so you can run tests from your environment if you prefer.
[00:06:31] Derek: Nice. for model variants, do you support automatic fallback if a preferred model is out of capacity?
[00:06:36] Samir: Yes, smart routing can fall back to compatible model variants with configurable policies — important for reliability. We'll surface fallbacks in the trace logs.
[00:06:45] Ava: For success criteria we also want to track quality regressions — who is responsible for that evaluation?
[00:06:50] Jordan: You (Stratus) will provide the gold eval set and acceptance thresholds; Redwood will run the eval and produce a report. If quality is below threshold we iterate on prompt tuning or suggest alternate model profiles.
[00:06:59] Maria: Anything about encryption keys — can we use our KMS?
[00:07:03] Jordan: Yes for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted we have provider-managed keys but can support Bring-Your-Own-KMS in Private deployments. We'll include the integration guide.
[00:07:12] Derek: On observability — we'd like token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards.
[00:07:18] Samir: Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token breakdowns, and traces. For POC we can enable a dashboard and share read-only access.
[00:07:26] Ava: Great. let's recap next steps.
[00:07:29] Jordan: Recap: Jordan sends POC proposal + pricing and NDA by Friday (2026-06-27). Samir will send benchmark harness, docker example, and OpenAI-compatible endpoint samples by 2026-06-29. Stratus (Ava/Derek) will share prompts, eval set, and QPS numbers by 2026-06-29 and confirm success criteria by 2026-06-30. Then technical kickoff week of 2026-07-06. Anyone want to add?
[00:07:49] Maria: Please include SOC2 summary and KMS guide in the package.
[00:07:54] Jordan: Will include.
[00:07:56] Ava: Sounds good. thanks all.
[00:07:59] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up.
